# Porphyromonas gingivals Mta1 and regulation Streptococcus mitis (Park et al., 2006). However, very little is known about regulatory mechanisms of mfal expression. In this study, it is demonstrated that Fimk is a positive regulator of Mfal expression. Evidence is provided that unlike FimR-dependent fimA expression, Fimk regulates mfal expression by directly binding to the promoter region of m/al. Materials and methods Bacterial strains and growth conditions The bacterial strains and plasmids used in this study are listed in 'lable 1. Porphyromonas gingivalis 33 277 and its derivatives were grown from frozen stocks in trypticase soy broth (TSB) or on TSB blood agar plates, supplemented with yeast extract (1 mg ml.'), hemin (5 pgml.) and menadione (1 ug ml.'), at 37°C in an anaerobic chamber (85% No, 10% H›, 5% CO,). Escherichia coli DH5x was the host for plasmids, and grown in Luria-Bertani (I.B) broth at 37°C. Antibiotics were used, when appropriate, at the following concentrations: gentamicin (100 pg mL), erythromycin (5 pg ml. '), ampicillin (50 ug ml. '), kanamycin (50 pg mL) and tetracycline (10 pg mL"). Construction of the fimR mutant An insertional fimR mutant was constructed by allelic replacement. Briefly, the fimR gene was amplified by PCR using primers fimRF and fimRR (Table 2) and cloned into pCRII-TOPO (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA) to give rise to a pFR plasmid (Table 1). A 2.1-kb ermF-ermAM cassette (Hetcher et al., 1995) was amplified using plasmid pVA3000 as a template and ErmF and Ermk as primers, which introduced Ndel sites at both ends of the PCR product. The ermf-ermAM cassette was then inserted into the fimk gene cloned in plasmid pFR. The resulting plasmids pFRE Table 1. Strains and plasmids used in this study

Electroporation was carried out by a modification of the procedure of Fletcher et al. (1995). Porphyromonas gingivalis 33277 competent cells were obtained by suspending early-log-phase cells in electroporation buffer (10% glycerol, 1.0mM MgCh). The cells were incubated with the linearized plasmid and were pulsed with a Bio-Rad gene pulser (Hercules, CA) at 2.5 kV. The cells were then immediately added to the TSB, and incubated anaerobically for 16h. The fimk mutants (FRE) resulting from a double-cross-over recombination were selected on Trypticase soy agar plates containing erythromycin (5 pg mL-*). The insertional mutation was confirmed by PCR analysis. RNA isolation and qPCR Porphyromonas gingivalis strains were grown anaerobically on Trypticase soy agar plates at 37°C for 48 h. Porphyromonas gingivals cells were collected and mixed in Trizol Reagent (Invitrogen). The RNA in the supernatant was then purified using an RNeasy mini spin column (Qiagen, Valencia, CA). To minimize contamination with genomic DNA, RNA samples were digested on the column with KNase-free DNase. The total RNA was tested using an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer to insure the quality of the samples. Gene expression was measured using the Quanti lect SYBR Green reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) Kit (Qiagen) and the iCycler iQ real-time detection system (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Inc.) according to the manufacturer's instructions. The primers for the fimA gene were fimAF and fimAR, and for the mal gene were mfalF and mfalR. Expression of the 165 KNA gene and rgpA (a gene encoding for arginine-gingipain) were tested as a control to normalize samples for variations in sample volume loading. Amplification reactions consisted of a reverse transcription cycle at 50°C for 30 min, an initial activation at 95°C. for 10 min, and 40 cycles of 94°C. for 15 s, FEMS Mkrobiol Lett 271 (2007) 214-221 o 2007 Federation of European Microbiological Societies Pubished by Blackwel Pubishing Ltd.
